summary: We built a burning activity calendar from NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspots that merges MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS 375 m (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) records from 2000 to 2026 into one series. A Python pipeline converts VIIRS detections into Terra-equivalent hotspots, using ratios learned per region, month of year and day/night on years when Terra's orbit was nominal, and switches to VIIRS only after Terra's overpass time drifted. It outputs a static data pack per 537 km² block and day, with gaps, near-real-time data and persistent sources flagged. A client-side web application reads the pack, lets the user select an area (box, polygon, centre and radius, or country), and shows a year-by-month calendar, the current month against the historical median, anomalies, critical periods and daily charts, with CSV export. The sensor no longer matters for the comparison, so emergency managers, land managers and scientists can see which months and years burned most and whether the current month is unusual.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

  • Input: FIRMS CSV archive, MODIS Terra/Aqua (1 km) and VIIRS 375 m: 667 files, 55.27 GB, 2000-11-01 to 2026-11-14.
  • Processing: detections are summed on the MODIS 1 km sinusoidal grid per 25×25-cell block (537 km², equal-area) and day. Days below 0.6 × the ±7-day median are flagged as gaps, not zero fire. The Terra-based period ends after a 20+ min overpass-time shift lasting 3 months.
  • Harmonized series H (Terra-equivalent hotspots): Terra alone before VIIRS; 0.5 Terra + 0.5 VIIRS-equivalent while Terra is nominal; VIIRS-equivalent after drift. VIIRS-equivalent = VIIRS pixel count × ratio f[month of year, 556 km tile, day/night], fitted on 2012–2021 with shrinkage world → 24 zones → tile; NOAA-20/21 are scaled to Suomi NPP per zone.
  • Output: static pack (192 gzip shards, 335 MB); the browser computes calendar, anomalies (log2 ratio, median/MAD z-score, percentile), P90 critical periods and three CSV exports.

Tech Stack

  • Pipeline: Python 3, NumPy, pandas, Shapely; Google Colab, Google Drive.
  • Web: vanilla JavaScript (ES modules), Canvas 2D map, SVG charts, DecompressionStream, Web Crypto (SHA-256 shard check); no framework, backend or external library.
  • Tests: Node.js tests (126 checks), 63 headless-browser UI checks; page numbers match an independent re-sum from shards up to rounding (synthetic and real-subset packs).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Users: early-warning and emergency responders, land managers, scientists. Problem: Terra's overpass drift mixes sensor change with fire change (H exceeds Terra counts by 5.0 % in 2022 and 39.4 % in 2026), and FIRMS ended Suomi NPP delivery on 2 Nov 2026. Result: consistent records per area, current month versus history, CSV download.

Creativity & Key Considerations

  • A single global VIIRS→MODIS factor was rejected: in leave-one-year-out tests on the full archive (2012–2021) it gave 38 % median error per zone-month, a ratio varying by region and month of year 9 %.
  • Calibration uses pixel counts, not FRP (NOAA-21 FRP differs by 11–14 %).
  • Measured on the full build (leave-one-year-out, 2012–2021, median error of the VIIRS estimate against Terra per month): 2.0 % world, 6.5 % zone, 13.5 % tile; 80 % of tile-months within ±30 %. The interface shows the 13.5 %.
  • Limits: the ratio is assumed stable over 2012–2021; extracts lack the type field, so persistent sources (cells detecting on 20+ days a year) are split out as Hp; near-real-time months are provisional.
